metadata.title: The second Bougard-Joret line up to order 24: an exhaustive check and the extremal graphs
metadata.description:
Let f(n, α, k) be the least number of edges of a k-connected graph with n vertices and independence number α. Bougard and Joret conjectured f(n, α, k) = t(n, α) + ⌈kα/2⌉ for n > kα, where t(n, α) counts the edges of α disjoint balanced cliques. Das and Gupta refuted the other line of the conjecture, and Didin has announced a proof of the lower bound in this line. We give an independent exhaustive check of it.

At every one of the 53 triples with α ≥ 3, k ≥ 3 and n ≤ 24 outside the range that Bougard and Joret's Proposition 8 settles, f equals the conjectured value, by complete enumeration of about 6.2 billion candidate graphs with nauty's generator, an independence prune proved sound and an exact filter. For seven pairs (α, k), including (5, 3), (4, 4) and (3, 6), the window ends by order 24, which settles the second line there for every n. A validation suite tests every component at the parameters used in production: the binaries rebuild byte for byte, 26,005 filter decisions and 27,132 prune decisions agree with an independent implementation, and the generator's splitting and counts agree with known values.

We list every extremal graph at 35 triples. Those that split into α cliques have the structure of Bougard and Joret's construction; 40 cannot be covered by α cliques, all with k = 3 and α odd. Conditional on Didin's main theorem, such graphs occur only at k = 3 with α odd and n ≤ 4α − 1, or at six small triples, and the data match this. Two building blocks recovered from the data give, for every odd α and every 3α < n ≤ 4α − 1, an explicit 3-connected graph with the conjectured number of edges, independence number α and no partition into α cliques; it is extremal at order 24 and below, and everywhere if Didin's theorem holds.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/combinatorics/bougard-joret/experiments, EXP-005 to EXP-013).
metadata.version_notes: Full rewrite. Order 24 completed (all 53 open-window triples with n <= 24 equal the conjectured value); seven pairs (alpha, k) settled for every n; methods with algorithms and soundness proofs; a validation suite at the production parameters; the complete extremal graphs at 35 triples, 40 of them without a partition into alpha cliques; a proposition, conditional on Didin's main theorem, locating such graphs; and an explicit construction of them for every odd alpha. Correction: versions 0.01 and 0.02 described the second line as open outside Bougard and Joret's range without citing Didin's preprint (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22831382, under review), which claims its lower bound for every n > k alpha; this version cites it and positions the enumeration as an independent check.
